headline: Self-Building Labs builds missing laboratory capabilities around a scientific goal
summary: Bai et al. describe a self-building laboratory system that starts from a scientific goal and an existing lab description, then constructs missing digital-twin components, robot/device skills and experimental workflows. Their arXiv v1 reports one physical cadmium-sulfide quantum-dot workflow: the system prepared a 96-well plate through 236 liquid-handler commands and 19 robotic transfer stages, with human approval and live sensing. The paper also demonstrates coordination across robots and multiple workstations in simulation. This is a source-reported prototype result, not evidence of general-purpose autonomous science: the authors state that successive-cycle performance, reduced engineering effort and reduced human intervention remain to be measured; they also report cases where device failures were not observable without human expertise.
